title: ALMA Spatially Resolved Dense Molecular Gas Survey of Nearby Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxies
question: How do HCN-to-HCO+ J=3-2 flux ratios, dense gas mass and vibrationally excited HCN vary within a uniformly selected sample of nearby ULIRGs, and do they reveal buried AGNs?

data.angular_resolution: 0.1''-0.2'' (150-530 pc) for most; 0.6''-0.8'' for two sources

evidence.quote: Col.(12): Infrared-spectroscopically estimated bolometric contribution of AGNs (in %) by (cite: nar10).

what.value: Pre-ALMA interferometric CO J=1-0 total molecular masses

evidence.quote: from pre-ALMA interferometric CO J=1–0 observations (cite: eva00; eva02)
Col.(11): Optical spectroscopic classification by (cite: vei99).

what.value: HCN/HCO+ J=3-2 results for three Cycle 2/3 ULIRGs

recipe.method: uvcontsub then clean to make continuum and line cubes from calibrated data
Gaussian fits to spectra at continuum peak; moment 0/1/2 maps; imfit for deconvolved sizes; spectra in 1-2'' apertures
Ratios of Gaussian fluxes for nuclear beam and integrated spectra; ratio maps from moment 0 where HCO+ >~3 sigma
Line luminosity (Solomon & Vanden Bout) times alpha_HCN
assumptions: alpha_HCN=10 (range 6-40), optically thick thermalized; alpha_CO=1.5 for CO J=2-1 total mass

recipe.method: Integrated continuum flux vs Herschel/IRAS extrapolation; free-free from L_FIR formula with Te=10^4 K
